title: Explain account-summary 5xx bursts during instance replacements

sources.claim: If a service's containers exceed the total container memory limit, the instance is terminated and requests still processing on it end with HTTP 500; the in-memory filesystem uses instance memory. The fixture's 1 GiB limit is explicitly configured, not the 512 MiB default.

A failed liveness probe shuts the container down with SIGKILL, remaining requests end with HTTP 503 and autoscaling starts a new instance; only 2XX/3XX responses within the timeout succeed. Defaults are failureThreshold 3, periodSeconds 10, timeoutSeconds 1; liveness probing starts after the startup probe succeeds, and repeated failures make Cloud Run limit restarts. The page does not say where probe failures are logged.

Documents the memory-termination message ('...was found to be using too much memory and was terminated'), says to look for it in varlog/system, and lists HTTP 500 or 503 for that case; documents a liveness log example ('LIVENESS HTTP probe failed 1 time consecutively for container CONTAINER_NAME on port 8080.') and that the instance is shut down. Message wording and the per-arm status codes are fixture observations and are not graded; the case rests on the paired termination, probe and memory records.

Instances that exceed their memory limit are terminated; Google suggests raising allocated memory for out-of-memory errors. In this case a limit change is an application-owner decision under approval, not a diagnosed cause fix.

Cloud Run container/memory/utilizations is a distribution across container instances, container/instance_count is split by active/idle state, and request_count carries a response_code_class label; each is sampled every 60 s and may be invisible for up to 120 s, so the fixture's metric coverage ends before capture time.

Cloud Run writes request logs, container stdout/stderr logs and platform system logs to varlog/system; cloud_run_revision labels identify project, location, service and revision, and instanceId maps to one instance as the service scales. Fixture cohorts and searches are authored observations.

a.conclusion: Instances of 00058-tqd exceeded the configured 1 GiB memory limit and were terminated; each 5xx burst is the in-flight requests on a terminating instance, followed by a replacement start. The configured liveness probe is not shown shutting instances down, and account-ledger reports baseline health. What consumes the memory is unproven.

b.conclusion: The configured HTTP liveness probe on /healthz failed three consecutive times on each affected instance, and Cloud Run shut those instances down; each 5xx burst is the in-flight requests on that instance, followed by a replacement start. /healthz answered in 2–3 s against a 1 s timeout while memory stayed near baseline. Why the health handler slowed is unproven.
